Parent conversation handoff summary:
Parent conversation handoff summary
Summary model: openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini
Source items: 79

Overview:
Parent conversation focused on assessing remaining gaps in the Support Bundle Investigator repo against the hiring PDF and PRD v2, after a large Phase 7 implementation landed. The repo already appears to satisfy most core product requirements (CLI-first, local-first, evidence-backed diagnosis, heuristic + AI paths, Markdown/HTML/JSON output, traceability, seeded scenarios), so follow-on work should prioritize reviewer confidence, stronger evals, observability, robustness, and documentation consistency rather than core feature completion.

Settled decisions:
- The project is effectively past core feature completeness; the remaining work is mainly proof, polish, and confidence-building.
- The strongest next step is to build a more explicit eval matrix covering scenario, expected top diagnosis, evidence, confidence band, heuristic vs AI results, and spec recommendations.
- AI-mode behavior is valuable but needs reproducible regression proof via recorded/replayed cassettes or a canonical AI eval corpus.
- Documentation should be cleaned up so current-complete state is not contradicted by stale roadmap/gap docs.
- Privacy/sensitive-data assurance should be treated as a differentiating trust feature and validated with tests, especially around secret handling and redaction guidance.

Constraints / must-remember items:
- README/visible repo surface should make completion obvious; a demo video link is considered a key missing deliverable.
- Current golden/e2e coverage is narrower than the feature set; several capabilities are unit-tested but under-demonstrated in scenario/e2e form.
- Observability is currently coarse and should be extended to include retrieval breakdowns, token/cost usage, merge/suppression reasons, and confidence deltas.
- Need to preserve local-first and no-required-network behavior as the default.
- Avoid relying on generic LLM summarization; the product must remain evidence- and contradiction-driven.
- Any changes to docs must avoid confusing reviewers about whether the project is complete or still in progress.

Open questions:
- Where is the demo video hosted, and should the repo/README be updated to link it prominently?
- Which additional seeded scenarios should be added first to cover under-demonstrated investigators (e.g. network policy, node taints/MemoryPressure, Helm release failures)?
- Should AI evals be added via replayable cassettes in CI, and if so what minimal corpus size is sufficient?
- What exact observability fields should be added to trace output to make diagnosis, evaluation, and demoing easier?
- Should stale roadmap/gap content be split into separate completed vs future-work docs, or just re-labeled with a clear historical disclaimer?
- How should sensitive-data safety be proved end-to-end so reports/prompts demonstrably avoid leaking secret values?

Use this handoff as background context. If it conflicts with the explicit task below or the current repository state, prioritize the explicit task and repo state.

Plan overview:
{
  "goal": "Improve evals, observability, and robustness across the Support Bundle Investigator: build a real eval scorecard across all scenarios, add AI replay/cassette evals, expand scenario corpus for newer investigators, enrich trace.json with seed/retrieval/confidence telemetry, add a debug mode with per-finding provenance, add cost/latency/model summaries for AI runs, and add robustness tests for corrupt/partial/oversized bundles, stress/perf benchmarks, and sensitive-data leakage.",
  "totalSteps": 16,
  "stepTitles": [
    "1. Expand eval scorecard: add ghost-service and multi-namespace-retrieval to GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS",
    "2. Add new scenario fixtures: network-policy-deny and node-taint-memory-pressure",
    "3. Add new scenario fixture: helm-release-failure",
    "4. Build eval scorecard JSON reporter and summary test",
    "5. Wire CassetteRecorder into the LLM execution path for record/replay",
    "6. AI cassette eval test: replay-based golden eval using wired path",
    "7. Enrich InvestigationTrace with seed, retrieval, and confidence telemetry",
    "8. Add per-finding provenance to Finding type and populate in investigators",
    "9. Add AI cost/latency/model summary to trace and report",
    "10. Add --debug CLI flag that emits enriched trace and provenance",
    "11. Robustness: corrupt and partial bundle tests",
    "12. Robustness: oversized bundle guard test",
    "13. Robustness: sensitive-data leakage tests",
    "14. Performance benchmark test for pipeline throughput",
    "15. Wire enriched trace fields into JSON and Markdown report output",
    "16. Final integration pass: build, lint, and full test suite green"
  ]
}

Step 1: Expand eval scorecard: add ghost-service and multi-namespace-retrieval to GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS
{
  "id": "step-1",
  "title": "Expand eval scorecard: add ghost-service and multi-namespace-retrieval to GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS",
  "description": "In `test/golden/expectations.ts`, add ScenarioExpectation entries for the existing `ghost-service` and `multi-namespace-retrieval` fixture scenarios. These scenarios already have fixture data in `test/fixtures/scenarios/` but no golden expectations. Define `topFindingMustMatch`, `topFindingSeverity`, `topFindingMinConfidence`, `mustCiteEvidence`, `mustNotHallucinate`, `rootCauseMustMatch`, and `mustMentionIdentifiers` for each. The existing `golden-eval.test.ts` auto-iterates `GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS`, so these will be tested automatically. Run the pipeline heuristic-only (noAi: true) against both scenarios first in a scratch test to determine the actual finding patterns, then set expectations to match. Follow the existing expectation pattern style exactly.",
  "requiredChecks": [
    "lint",
    "typecheck",
    "unit"
  ]
}

This is relay round 2. Another agent has already worked on this step.
Review what has been done, fix any issues, and make improvements.

Previous agent's notes:
Reviewed:
- `test/golden/expectations.ts`
- heuristic-only pipeline behavior for `ghost-service` and `multi-namespace-retrieval`

Changed:
- Added a `GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS` entry for `ghost-service`
- Added a `GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS` entry for `multi-namespace-retrieval`

Notes:
- I first ran the pipeline in heuristic-only mode against both fixtures to see the actual finding shapes.
- `ghost-service` currently ranks a `CrashLoopBackOff` symptom first, with the cross-namespace DNS/service mismatch as a strong secondary finding, so the expectation allows either top-title pattern while still requiring the `api-service.staging`/`staging` evidence.
- `multi-namespace-retrieval` currently ranks the concrete DNS failure from `migration-pod` first, so the expectation is anchored on DNS/wrong-host/migration patterns and requires evidence/identifiers spanning the `database` and `monitoring` namespaces.
- I used a temporary scratch test to inspect findings, then removed it.

Checks run:
- `npm run lint` ✅
- `npm run typecheck` ✅
- `npm run unit` ✅

Assessment:
- Step 1 is complete.
- The new expectations match current heuristic behavior and the existing golden eval suite passes with them.

Overview:
Parent conversation focused on assessing remaining gaps in the Support Bundle Investigator repo against the hiring PDF and PRD v2, after a large Phase 7 implementation landed. The repo already appears to satisfy most core product requirements (CLI-first, local-first, evidence-backed diagnosis, heuristic + AI paths, Markdown/HTML/JSON output, traceability, seeded scenarios), so follow-on work should prioritize reviewer confidence, stronger evals, observability, robustness, and documentation consistency rather than core feature completion.

Settled decisions:
- The project is effectively past core feature completeness; the remaining work is mainly proof, polish, and confidence-building.
- The strongest next step is to build a more explicit eval matrix covering scenario, expected top diagnosis, evidence, confidence band, heuristic vs AI results, and spec recommendations.
- AI-mode behavior is valuable but needs reproducible regression proof via recorded/replayed cassettes or a canonical AI eval corpus.
- Documentation should be cleaned up so current-complete state is not contradicted by stale roadmap/gap docs.
- Privacy/sensitive-data assurance should be treated as a differentiating trust feature and validated with tests, especially around secret handling and redaction guidance.

Constraints / must-remember items:
- README/visible repo surface should make completion obvious; a demo video link is considered a key missing deliverable.
- Current golden/e2e coverage is narrower than the feature set; several capabilities are unit-tested but under-demonstrated in scenario/e2e form.
- Observability is currently coarse and should be extended to include retrieval breakdowns, token/cost usage, merge/suppression reasons, and confidence deltas.
- Need to preserve local-first and no-required-network behavior as the default.
- Avoid relying on generic LLM summarization; the product must remain evidence- and contradiction-driven.
- Any changes to docs must avoid confusing reviewers about whether the project is complete or still in progress.

Open questions:
- Where is the demo video hosted, and should the repo/README be updated to link it prominently?
- Which additional seeded scenarios should be added first to cover under-demonstrated investigators (e.g. network policy, node taints/MemoryPressure, Helm release failures)?
- Should AI evals be added via replayable cassettes in CI, and if so what minimal corpus size is sufficient?
